problem.statement: The current local free-roaming dog population is not continuously enumerated by the periodic national survey system.

practical.statement: Taiwan estimates the national free-roaming dog population every two years using a photographic capture survey method; the 2024 estimate was 141,584 dogs.

academic.statement: Free-ranging dog abundance estimates can be biased when detection probability, individual identification, registration, or population closure assumptions are inadequately handled.
Photographic mark-recapture and capture-recapture methods can use repeated individual observations to estimate free-roaming dog abundance under explicit assumptions.

implementations.statement: Talea is a street-survey system that records roaming animal sightings, characteristics, routes, survey areas, and geolocated observations.

findings.interpretation: The Ministry of Agriculture cautioned that the 2024 national decline relative to 2022 was not statistically significant.
findings.why: This qualification changes how the practical observation can be interpreted.
findings.next_check: Review sampling, significance and whether a causal interpretation is supported.

findings.interpretation: Talea is a street-survey system that records roaming animal sightings, characteristics, routes, survey areas, and geolocated observations. However: ICAM's Talea guide says a sighting cannot include an animal photograph; the app can record textual notes. The scientific method requires: Repeated sightings need reliable individual reconciliation before they can support individual-aware population estimation.
findings.why: The implementation limitation interrupts a named requirement of the linked scientific method.
findings.next_check: Verify whether talea can actually satisfy: Repeated sightings need reliable individual reconciliation before they can support individual-aware population estimation.

problem.statement: Immigration and replenishment can undermine fertility-control effects in an open free-roaming dog population.

practical.statement: Miaoli reported about 7,400 roaming dogs in 2025 and stated that intensified capture and inspection were still being outpaced by abandonment, free-roaming owned dogs, and reproduction.

academic.statement: In Shoushan, modelling indicated that maintaining female sterilization above 75 percent could theoretically control the dog population, while roughly 50 to 100 incoming dogs per year could severely disrupt the TNR effect.

implementations.statement: Taiwan's 2026 community free-roaming dog management program prioritizes risk hotspots, female-dog source control, pet registration, sterilization, owner responsibility, and community participation.

findings.interpretation: Taiwan's 2026 community free-roaming dog management program prioritizes risk hotspots, female-dog source control, pet registration, sterilization, owner responsibility, and community participation.
findings.why: The reviewed graph links a documented program to this problem but provides no outcome-evaluation edge.
findings.next_check: Locate an independent intervention evaluation with a specified outcome, baseline and population.
